title: Singing at St. Alphonsus closing exercises
summary: Asked about the choir, he says he sang counter-melodies to The Holy City at school closing exercises under a teacher named Sokola.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Mr. Marocca, did you ever play, or not play, but sing or have anything to do with the St. Alphonsus choir?

No, I didn't. But I did sing at the closing exercise. And there was a man who used to teach us there, was named Sokola. His first name, I can't remember. But he used to put on the show for us. And we were singing the Holy City. Ta-da, ta-da, ta-da, ta-da, Hosanna, and so on. And I used to sing counter melodies against it. At that time I didn't know anything. I could show you on the piano how easy it is for me to get a melody. And many people say, how you put them together? Well, to me they come just like they come out the air. All I need is four notes or five notes to start on. And a chord construction to follow. And I can make a melody. And that's not only now. I've been doing that since I've been nine, ten years old.
